clue.text: Mutual connection in gracious story

blocks.note: 'Gracious!' and 'Cor!' are both exclamations of surprise
a relation is an account or narrative

explanation.surface: Someone finds a shared bond in a kindly tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gracious' reads as an adjective for the story but is an exclamation; COR is a British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A correlation is a reciprocal relationship between two things, each varying with the other.

clue.text: Empire that's been stuffed

blocks.note: first meaning: the Turkish empire ruled from Constantinople
second meaning: an upholstered, padded low seat or footstool

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a defeated empire; the second half describes a padded piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Turkish imperial state shares its name with a cushioned footstool, both called after the dynasty founder Osman.

clue.text: Pure nonsense, board trustworthy

indicators.note: nonsense is jumbled sense, so the preceding word's letters come out scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a board is a table, as in 'bed and board'

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses as rubbish the idea that a company board can be trusted.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reputable has a good reputation and so can be relied on.

clue.text: Greatly enjoy leading Formula One race, say?

blocks.note: first meaning: to relish eagerly, like a cat with milk
second meaning: read literally

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful literal reading: being one circuit ahead of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: To lap up praise or attention is an idiom for relishing it with enthusiasm.

clue.text: Chunky rolls with cheese that's fine and crisp

indicators.note: something that rolls over turns end to end, so the word for chunky runs backwards

blocks.note: chunky means stout or fat
feta is a Greek cheese

explanation.surface: A recipe for bread rolls filled with cheese, judged fine and crisp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chunky rolls' looks like bread; 'rolls' is a verb turning the word for chunky round.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp, smooth woven fabric, typically silk, so it is something fine and crisp.

clue.text: Asian craft making capital in central Wyoming

indicators.note: central asks for the core of the state's name, dropping its outer letters
in places the capital inside the letters taken from the state

blocks.note: the middle three of the seven letters
Riga is the capital of Latvia

explanation.surface: A US state hosts the production of an Asian handicraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of folding paper into shapes, a traditional Asian craft.

clue.text: Change medium, it getting hard for metalworker

indicators.note: getting means acquiring something extra, so the next part is added on after

blocks.note: coppers are small coins, loose change
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium
taken as written
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A séance where one psychic is swapped for another who proves tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change medium' reads as an instruction to swap; 'Change' is coins and 'medium' a size.
explanation.definitionFit: A coppersmith is a craftsman who works copper, a kind of metalworker.

clue.text: Hand back on pivot

blocks.note: re means on or concerning
to pivot is to turn

explanation.surface: A hand swivels backwards on a hinge.
explanation.definitionFit: To return something is to give it back to its owner.

clue.text: Pose with ten performing old dance

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters are put through their paces into a new routine

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A troupe of ten strikes a pose while doing a period dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-step was a ballroom dance popular in the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Advertisement featured by flier

blocks.note: a puff is a promotional plug
something featured is in it

explanation.surface: An advert appears on a printed leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' suggests a handbill to go with the advertisement, but it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The puffin is a seabird, and anything that flies can be called a flier.

clue.text: Suntan I worked on, agony briefly

indicators.note: worked means kneaded or reshaped, so those letters take a new order
in a down answer, on means the next part is placed after the first

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
hell is agony, torment

explanation.surface: A sunbather sums up the painful sunburn they got working on a tan.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something in a nutshell means putting it concisely, in very few words.

clue.text: Drop shade with force

blocks.note: plum is a dark purple colour
the Met is London's Metropolitan Police force

explanation.surface: A blind or lampshade is pulled down hard.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met is the usual name for London's police service.
explanation.definitionFit: To plummet is to fall or drop steeply and fast.

clue.text: Man bottling wine very early in the morning

indicators.note: bottling means holding something inside, so one word sits within the other

blocks.note: a chess piece is called a man, and the pawn is the humblest
red is a type of wine

explanation.surface: A man filling bottles with wine at the crack of dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Predawn describes the hours just before daybreak, the earliest part of the morning.

clue.text: Approach career with it

blocks.note: to career is to rush or run headlong
with it means fashionable, in

explanation.surface: Advice to tackle one's working life in a trendy way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' is a verb, to rush, not a profession.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-in is the approach or lead-up to an event, such as the run-in to an election.

clue.text: One pub joining another in welcoming a savage

indicators.note: joining means linking up side by side, so the two items are placed next to each other
welcoming means taking in a guest, so one item is held inside the other

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
a second pub
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two linked pubs let in a wild, uncivilised customer.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbarian is a brutal, uncivilised person, which a savage is too.

clue.text: Drop journalist into protest

indicators.note: into tells us one word is pushed inside the other

blocks.note: a ruction is a noisy row or protest
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A reporter is told to go and join a demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop' reads as a verb but works as the noun, a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A reduction is a decrease in amount, so a drop, as in a price drop.

clue.text: Area of expertise for bloke in East Midlands town

blocks.note: a bloke is a man; 'for bloke' makes it possessive, man's
one's field is one's specialism

explanation.surface: A man's specialism lies in a Midlands town.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces read 'man's field', with 'for bloke' supplying the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Mansfield is a market town in Nottinghamshire, in the English East Midlands.

clue.text: A lot, by inference? I don't think so

blocks.note: first meaning: a lot is plainly not a small amount, read literally
second meaning: a firm denial, not at all

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the literal reading: if something is a lot, it is by inference not small.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a colloquial way of saying 'not at all', a flat refusal or denial.

clue.text: Foil work, perhaps, putting up barriers

blocks.note: first meaning: the sport of swordplay, of which foil is one weapon
second meaning: erecting fences

explanation.walkthrough: 'Foil' suggests kitchen or metal foil, or thwarting; it is the light sword.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names both the sport of swordplay and the job of putting up fences around land.

clue.text: Strong drink

blocks.note: first meaning: sturdy, robust
second meaning: a dark beer such as porter

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase about a potent drink; the words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for sturdy or brave and the name of a dark heavy beer.

clue.text: Recognise monarch hunting

blocks.note: to see is to recognise or perceive
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: Spotting the sovereign out at a royal hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeking means searching or looking for something, as in hunting for it.

clue.text: Old hat in good shape for suit, say

blocks.note: old hat means outdated, out of fashion
being fit means being in good shape

explanation.surface: An old hat still looking smart enough to go with a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hat' looks like headgear but is an idiom for unfashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: A suit is one example of a set of clothes worn together, which is an outfit.

clue.text: Enormous junk in attic

indicators.note: junk is a jumble of rubbish, so the words that follow are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A vast amount of clutter stored up in the loft.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic means gigantic, from the Titans, the giants of Greek myth.

clue.text: Best put paper under contract at first

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it
in a down answer, under means placed below, so the paper comes after

blocks.note: the opening letter
a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: Advice to sign the best writer to a deal first.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream is the best part of something, as in the cream of the crop.

clue.text: One pulling a fast one, did you say? That's very quick

indicators.note: asking what someone said points to how a word is pronounced rather than written

blocks.note: pulling a fast one is cheating, so this is a cheat

explanation.surface: Accusing someone of trickery, and remarking how fast they were.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the two words sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheetah is the fastest land animal, so it is a thing that is very quick.

clue.text: Boil half of eggs another way, please

indicators.note: half of asks for only part of the following word, here its front portion
done another way means the letters are arranged differently

blocks.note: taken as written
the first two of its four letters

explanation.surface: A request to cook some eggs differently, said politely.
explanation.definitionFit: To oblige someone is to do them a favour, so to please them.

clue.text: First language I rejected: Swahili finally embraced

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the letters run backwards
finally asks for the last letter of the word before it
embraced means held within, so the single letter goes inside

blocks.note: Latin is a language
taken as written
its last letter

explanation.surface: A student turns down Latin as a first language and takes up Swahili instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Initial means occurring at the beginning, so first.

clue.text: Engineer: worker needing time on platform

indicators.note: the remaining words are attached to the platform, so they follow it

blocks.note: a stage is a raised platform
to man is to staff, so a man is a worker
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: An engineer and a labourer wait their turn on a railway platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' looks like a job title but is a verb, to contrive.
explanation.definitionFit: To stage-manage events is to arrange them behind the scenes for effect, to engineer them.
